title: Central Bureau of Investigation v. Sudipto Sen & Debjani Mukherjee (Saradha Chit Fund Scam)
crime_type: Chit Fund Ponzi Scheme / Public Embezzlement / Political Corruption
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / High Court at Calcutta
source: Supreme Court of India & Indian Kanoon (doc/79261053)
ipc_sections: Section 409 IPC (Criminal breach of trust by merchant/agent)
Section 420 IPC (Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property)
Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act 1978
location: Kolkata, West Bengal & Bhubaneswar, Odisha, India
evidence: Collapse of 239 subsidiary companies registered under Saradha banner without genuine business operations or revenue streams
18-page signed confession letter written by Sudipto Sen naming influential political patrons before flight to Sonamarg, Kashmir
Banking audit documenting collection of over ₹2,500 crore from 1.7 million low-income depositors across East India
Forensic financial analysis showing redemption payments funded solely by incoming subscriptions from new depositors
modus_operandi: Constructed an elaborate multi-tiered pyramid collective investment scheme promising absurdly high interest returns of 15% to 50% disguised as timeshare holiday memberships, real estate bookings, and agro-bonds. Funded high-profile television channels, newspapers, and cultural events to cultivate an aura of untouchable prestige and political patronage.
personality_disorder: Parasitic sociopathy, pathological charm, and reckless financial predation on working-class citizens.
common_traits: Classic Ponzi payout mechanics (paying old investors with new funds)
Acquisition of media outlets and political proximity as defensive shields
Mass mobilization through commission-incentivized village agents
Abrupt collapse and midnight flight upon cash-flow exhaustion
summary: One of Eastern India largest financial frauds affecting 1.7 million depositors. Investigated by CBI under Supreme Court orders, leading to landmark rulings on regulatory oversight of non-banking financial companies.
